graphEvents.label: Which failure modes matter most for command surfacing
Non-doctor command-versus-skill ties have no precedence rule
Child sessions can start mutating commands without an ask
Command workflows can re-enter routing on their own writes

label: Command-versus-skill ambiguity is by construction for non-doctor commands: /speckit:plan returns command-spec-kit 0.82/0.20 and system-spec-kit 0.82/0.18, inside the 0.05 ambiguity margins, and the brief has no precedence rule.

Doctor bridges have a precedence rule non-doctor bridges lack: a typed doctor command puts its bridge first, passing doctor bridges sit after passing skills, and doctor bridges are removed before skill ambiguity is computed.

A dispatched child session is the highest unsafe-run risk: AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 pre-resolves Gate 3 and turns stop-for-yes into record-and-continue, so a child with a run brief can start a mutating command with no user to answer.

The routing loop risk is partly controlled: Gate 2 fires before every code or Markdown write and command workflows write, while directive dedup suppresses repeated briefs but not repeated routing decisions.
The only anti-self-recommendation control is a -0.25 penalty against the advisor's own ids on audit or explainer prompts; it does not stop a command workflow from routing back into the advisor.

Over-triggering is partly controlled by the -0.08 no-slash penalty and the read-only gate; the highest over-trigger surface is doctor lead_phrases, measured as disable comment hygiene gate leading with /doctor:git hooks.

The brief budget tolerates one command line and one policy marker; a third consequence line competes with the fixed directive block and ambiguity head inside the 120-token cap, so the order should be command, policy, consequence.

Recommended controls: a same-owner command-versus-skill precedence rule, child authority limited to read-only or add-only commands, a route-once guard per turn and command, a diagnostic-only lead-phrase allowlist, and the command-policy-consequence line order.

Evidence against a blanket command-first rule: in the measured /speckit:plan case the skill has the lower uncertainty, so the rule must be scoped to a command and its own owner skill rather than applied to every command-skill pair.
